title: Verifier‑Assisted versus One‑Shot LLM Intent→Configuration: A Paired NetOpsTraceBench Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed NetOpsTraceBench (study_id=rX4f7-1), a paired comparison of a one‑shot NL→configuration pipeline and a verifier‑assisted generate–validate–repair pipeline using gpt-5-mini, a deterministic NetOps validator, and Mininet‑style emulation. Planned: 1,200 paired intent→config episodes; completed: 1,199 pairs. Primary binary episode success (preregistered): validator accepts final config AND emulator shows no availability degradation above tolerance AND no automatic rollback. Results: baseline success = 1,196/1,199 (0.9974979149291076); guarded success = 1,199/1,199 (1.0000000000); paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002502085070892446. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0000, 0.005838198498748957] (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10,000). Repair was invoked 3 times; provider audit records hosted_model_call_event_count = 1,203 and model_calls_used = 1,203. The preregistered topology‑cluster breakdown (H3) was not executed as a confirmatory subgroup analysis; confirmatory analysis artifacts contain no per‑cluster inferential results (see analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json, execution/execution_manifest.json). Under these synthetic tasks and validator settings we find no statistically significant advantage for the verifier‑assisted pipeline; archived artifacts and execution accounting are provided for reproducible follow‑up and sensitivity studies.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent in natural language into executable device configurations for NetOps. Prior surveys and system papers argue that operational correctness and trustworthiness are properties of the full orchestration stack (model + verifier + provenance + sandboxed execution), and they promote generate–validate–repair (verifier‑assisted) architectures to reduce hazardous outputs. Despite conceptual support, preregistered, artifact‑rich, paired evidence that measures whether verifier assistance yields a meaningful operational improvement (rollback‑aware binary success) relative to one‑shot generation is scarce. We address this gap with NetOpsTraceBench: a preregistered, paired, emulator‑grounded study that asks whether a reproducible, workflow‑centered benchmark of paired intent→config episodes can detect an operationally meaningful advantage for verifier‑assisted pipelines.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and position papers frame LLMs for NetOps as components within broader AIOps workflows and repeatedly call for workflow‑centered evaluations that record full provider and validator traces, sandboxed execution, and rollback semantics [see cited records]. Generator+verifier loops appear in NL→formal/specification work and in topology‑compilation prototypes; demonstrations commonly show feasibility on constructed corpora but underscore sensitivity to task selection and verifier strictness. Empirical studies document LLM failure modes relevant to NetOps—hallucination, unit/semantic errors, overconfidence/miscalibration, provenance loss—and motivate guarded architectures that can catch many, but not all, errors. These prior findings motivated our preregistered paired design that archives raw outputs, validator traces, provider audit logs, and emulator results to make dependencies observable.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and primary estimand: The study was preregistered as NetOpsTraceBench (rX4f7-1; preregistration SHA‑256 = 77abe8b493bde44484e0b3d02cfd7f9ec1621ff7e7847889082ae177a7ed5712) and froze hypotheses, inclusion/exclusion rules, seeds, stopping rules, and the primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Task corpus and generation: 1,200 deterministic operator‑intent tasks were generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with frozen per‑task generation_seed values and split conceptually into two topology clusters (edge/core) of 600 tasks each as specified in the preregistration. Pipeline design and shared‑candidate semantics: we used a shared_initial_candidate design (generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate") so that baseline (one‑shot) and guarded (verifier‑assisted) episodes for each task started from the same LLM candidate; this isolates the verifier/repair step from generation variability. Model and orchestration: requested_model = gpt-5-mini via provider recorded as openai_responses; adapter orchestration = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model_configuration.json records max_output_tokens = 1500 and maximum_attempts_per_call = 1. Verifier and emulator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) performed canonical parsing and intent‑constraint validation; emulator preflight and execution instrumentation measured availability and rollback events. Contamination and exclusions: preregistered contamination thresholds and deterministic exclusion rules were applied; no contamination exclusions occurred for the confirmatory analysis. Analysis plan and documented analytic deviation: the preregistration specified a paired nonparametric test and bootstrap CI. Because outcomes were binary and highly concentrated, the archived confirmatory analysis executed an exact McNemar two‑sided test on discordant pairs and computed a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10,000); this analytic choice and its rationale are documented in archived artifacts.
sections.results: Execution accounting: planned episodes = 2,400 (1,200 pairs × 2 conditions); completed episodes = 2,398; failed_episode_count = 2; complete_pair_count = 1,199. Provider audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 1,203 (completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 1,202; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 1); model_calls_used = 1,203; stage_counts show shared_initial_generation = 1,200 and repair = 3. Primary confirmatory outcomes (archived analysis artifacts): analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv shows n11 = 1,196, n10 = 3, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. From these counts: baseline_success_count = 1,196/1,199 = 0.9974979149291076; guarded_success_count = 1,199/1,199 = 1.0; paired difference = 0.002502085070892446. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0000, 0.005838198498748957] (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10,000), archived in analysis/results.json and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. Repair invocation: repair calls were invoked in exactly three episodes (repair = 3) per execution/provider_calls and execution/scoring artifacts; most shared_initial_candidate outputs were accepted by the validator (validation_after.valid == true) and required no automated repair. Missingness and exclusions: analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 1,199; failed_baseline_episodes = 1; failed_guarded_episodes = 1; both_missing_pairs = 1. Preregistered H3 (topology‑cluster breakdown): the preregistration included H3 (paired breakdown across the two simulated topology clusters). The confirmatory analysis artifacts archived with this run do not contain per‑cluster inferential tables or per‑cluster McNemar tests; therefore H3 was not executed as a completed confirmatory subgroup analysis and is not reported here. Readers can inspect the primary artifacts at analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json, and execution/execution_manifest.json to reproduce the primary inference.
sections.discussion: Statistical and operational interpretation: the observed paired difference favors guarded (all discordant pairs favored guarded, n10=3, n01=0) but is too small, given near‑ceiling baseline performance, to reach preregistered inferential thresholds (exact McNemar p = 0.25; CI includes zero). The preregistered MDE was 5 percentage points; the observed absolute gain (~0.25 percentage points) is far below that target and the study therefore lacked power to resolve such a small effect under the chosen corpus and validator settings. Artifact diagnostics explain why repairs were rare: the deterministic task generator produced tasks with explicit required sequences and the deterministically configured validator accepted most initial candidates. Implications: when initial generation already satisfies deterministic verifier checks for well‑specified synthetic tasks, verifier scaffolding will be infrequently exercised and measured binary gains will be small. To evaluate verifier utility more sensitively, future work should increase task ambiguity/adversariality, vary verifier strictness, and test multiple LLM families. Reproducibility: all raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, task manifests, transformation manifests, execution logs, and analysis code (artifact_count = 8,408) are archived; key artifacts for reproducing the primary confirmatory result are analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/results.json, and execution/execution_manifest.json.
sections.conclusion: NetOpsTraceBench deployed a preregistered, paired, emulator‑grounded comparison of one‑shot and verifier‑assisted NL→config pipelines across 1,199 completed pairs. Under the synthetic task corpus, deterministic validator, and requested model gpt-5-mini, baseline generation achieved near‑ceiling success (≈99.75%); the guarded pipeline improved absolute success by ≈0.25 percentage points (paired difference = 0.0025020851) but this small effect is not statistically significant by the archived exact McNemar two‑sided test (p = 0.25) and the bootstrap CI includes zero. Repair was invoked only three times; provider audit records model_calls_used = 1,203. The preregistered topology cluster hypothesis (H3) was not executed as a confirmatory subgroup analysis and therefore is not reported beyond noting its absence in the archived confirmatory artifacts. All artifacts and seeds are archived to enable reproducible sensitivity studies that vary corpus difficulty, verifier strictness, and model families to identify conditions where verifier assistance yields operationally meaningful improvements.

limitations: Single model family tested (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across other LLMs or fine‑tuned variants.
Task corpus skew: synthetic/consented tasks yielded near‑ceiling baseline success (≈99.75%), limiting headroom and statistical power to detect practical improvements by guarded pipelines.

Emulator fidelity: Mininet‑style emulation and deterministic validators approximate production behavior but may not capture all deployment failure modes (routing convergence, vendor idiosyncrasies, transient telemetry).

Verifier configuration dependence: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 acceptance thresholds and parsing rules materially affect outcomes; different verifier strictness could change repair invocation rates and measured gains.

Analytic deviation documented: the preregistration specified a Wilcoxon signed‑rank paired procedure; the archived confirmatory analysis used an exact McNemar test because outcomes were binary. This deviation is recorded in the archived analysis artifacts.
Operational external validity: absence of heterogeneous vendor renderers, real production templates, and live rollouts constrain direct production generalization.

Preregistered topology cluster hypothesis (H3) was not executed as a completed confirmatory subgroup analysis; confirmatory artifacts do not contain per‑cluster inferential results and therefore per‑cluster conclusions are not reported here.
